description: Structured output of the validator agent.

contradictions.description: Subsets of individually feasible criteria that cannot hold together.

items.description: A subset of criterion ids whose conjunction admits no implementation.

criterionIds.description: The minimal subset of criterion ids that cannot all hold at once.
criterionIds.title: Criterionids

explanation.description: Why no single implementation satisfies that subset.
explanation.title: Explanation

items.title: Contradiction

contradictions.title: Contradictions

findings.description: Exactly one finding per dispatched criterion id, covering every id.

items.description:
One refuter finding about one criterion — the validator's raw output.

The refuter states the ``verdict`` and the evidence behind it: the
smallest repair that would settle the criterion, and what it
established.  Evidence is carried so a human can audit "supply a
Postgres instance", and so the sweep can ground the statement:
``classify_finding`` derives its own verdict from the evidence alone,
and a stated verdict the evidence does not derive is refused.

anyOf.description:
A demonstration of a criterion performed against the repo AT BASE.

Its existence is the claim that the refuter ran the criterion's own
check before any work: ``satisfied_at_base`` is an observed result,
never a prediction, and vacuity is read from it and nothing else.

command.description: The command you ran at the base ref to establish this.
command.title: Command

satisfiedAtBase.description: Whether the criterion already holds before any work is done.
satisfiedAtBase.title: Satisfiedatbase

anyOf.title: BaseDemonstration

baseDemonstration.description: Evidence that the criterion already holds at the base ref.

anyOf.description:
An assertion about the price of demonstrating a criterion.

``measurement`` is ``None`` when the cost was argued rather than
measured, and the refuter is told an argued cost may not carry a
verdict.  The sweep's derivation weighs the claim rather than reading
it past: an unmeasured claim and an affordable measurement are both
struck and support no repair; only a measured, uneconomic one
survives, and it is environment-side.

assertion.description: The cost the criterion is claimed to impose.
assertion.title: Assertion

anyOf.description:
A measurement of a demonstration that ACTUALLY RAN.

Its existence is the claim that the demonstration completed; a
demonstration a limit prevented from running has no instance of this
type at all.

affordable.description: Whether the measured cost is one an implementer can pay.
affordable.title: Affordable

observed.description: What the measurement returned, quoted from the output you ran.
observed.title: Observed

anyOf.title: CostMeasurement

measurement.description: The measurement backing the assertion; absent when none was taken.

anyOf.title: CostClaim

costClaim.description: A cost the criterion imposes, with the measurement behind it.

criterionId.description: The dispatched criterion's id, echoed exactly. Return one finding per dispatched id and invent none.
criterionId.title: Criterionid

anyOf.description:
The classes the drafter is instructed never to emit.

The instruction is prose addressed to a model, so instances reach the
sweep.  Five of the six describe criteria nothing in the run can
grade, and one of those reaching the loop fails every iteration and
burns the budget proving a defect that predates iteration one — the
refuter returns ``infeasible`` for them and the class is recorded here.

``literal_count`` is the exception: the count can be hit, so it is not
a feasibility fault.  It is FLAGGED and forced to ``soft_signal``.
anyOf.title: ForbiddenCriterionClass

forbiddenClass.description: The forbidden criterion class this one falls into, when it does.

missingResource.description: The file, symbol, binding or rule that must be SUPPLIED before the criterion can be decided. Its absence is a lack in the environment, not a fault in the criterion's text: it pairs with unverifiable and environment_supply, never with infeasible.
missingResource.title: Missingresource

pinnedLiterals.description: Exact counts, paths or formatting the criterion pins that a correct refactor may change.
pinnedLiterals.title: Pinnedliterals

refutation.description: Evidence an implementer could not overturn, for an infeasible verdict. An unproven suspicion is not a refutation.
refutation.title: Refutation

smallestRepair.description: The smallest repair that would settle the criterion, bound to the verdict: feasible names none, infeasible names criterion_text (the criterion's own text must change), unverifiable names environment_supply (something absent must be supplied to the environment — not a text change). Any other pairing is refused.
smallestRepair.title: RepairKind

undeclaredSwitchArms.description: Cases the criterion names that the declared type does not have. Naming ANY arm here makes the criterion infeasible — the fault is in the criterion's own text, and nothing supplied to a runner makes an arm exist. A type that could not be found at all is a missingResource, not an undeclared arm.
undeclaredSwitchArms.title: Undeclaredswitcharms

verdict.description: Feasible, infeasible, or unverifiable — never folded into each other.
verdict.title: CriterionVerdict

findings.title: Findings
